research_question: Does NLRP3 inflammasome activation drive pyroptosis and acute kidney injury in sepsis, and which biomarkers predict progression?
scope: Translational nephrology; human cohorts and mouse models of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury

records.title: NLRP3 inflammasome activation drives tubular pyroptosis in septic acute kidney injury
records.abstract: NLRP3 inflammasome activation and gasdermin D cleavage caused tubular pyroptosis in mice with sepsis, and NLRP3 deletion reduced acute kidney injury.
records.text: NLRP3 inflammasome activation increased caspase-1 activity and gasdermin D cleavage in tubular epithelial cells. Genetic deletion of NLRP3 reduced pyroptosis and preserved kidney function in septic mice.

records.title: Urinary NLRP3 predicts progression of acute kidney injury in sepsis
records.abstract: In a prospective cohort, higher urinary NLRP3 predicted progression of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis.
records.text: Among 120 patients with sepsis, urinary NLRP3 at admission predicted progression of acute kidney injury and need for renal replacement therapy.

records.title: Gasdermin D cleavage and pyroptosis in sepsis-associated organ injury
records.abstract: Gasdermin D cleavage was associated with pyroptosis in sepsis, but not with acute kidney injury severity.
records.text: Plasma gasdermin D correlated with pyroptosis markers across organs. The association with acute kidney injury severity was weak and not significant after adjustment.
